SCHEDULE: {"1":"Finn","2":"Ivo","3":"Ann","4":"Gus","5":"Elif","6":"Dev","7":"Ben","8":"Cara","9":"Hana"}
CONFIDENCE: 97

The constraints force Finn < Elif < Cara < Hana with gaps of at least 3 between Finn and Elif and between Elif and Cara. That puts Cara at slot 7 or 8 and Hana at 8 or 9. Working through those cases, Hana = 8 and Cara = 7 leave no slot for Gus, and Hana = 9 with Cara = 7 fails on Ben and Elif. Hana = 9, Cara = 8, Dev = 6, Finn = 1, Elif = 5, Ben = 7 is the only assignment that works. I checked all 21 constraints against it.

The shared note's first line is self-contradictory (it says both "Finn first" and "Ivo first"). Its final reasoning, with Finn in slot 1, Ivo in slot 2, and Ann in slot 3, matches this solution.
